prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: receiving interface–outbound-load release. No explicit modes. Elements/items: Inbound Inspection Desk (Cinderbay): shipment/paperwork/trailer checks, inspection/damage/identifier/seal records; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note. Pallet Dimension Scanner (Moonquarry): measures height/width/length; checks configured/declared profiles; produces Oversize Load Advisory identifying exceeded storage/handling limits, not placement authorization. Inbound Pallet Buffer: accepted pallets. North Aisle Stacker Crane (Juniperwake): north-aisle storage/retrieval, configured travel limits. South Aisle Stacker Crane: assigned-aisle storage/retrieval, equivalent travel/access controls. East Transfer Conveyor/West Transfer Conveyor: eastern/western transfer approaches. Conveyor Line Controller: movement sequencing. Autonomous Forklift Fleet: authorized tasks/areas only. Yard Gate Controller (Velvetrook): access, vehicle/carrier/trailer/arrival records, cleared staging-to-door routing. Outbound Dispatch Sorter: sequencing. Outbound Checkweigh Scale: preshipment weights. Shipping Documentation Desk: outbound records. Warehouse Operations Supervisor: exceptions/priorities/recovery/receiving escalation/unresolved-allocation review. Warehouse Management System (Morrowglass): authoritative inventory/status/location/eligibility/expected shipments; authorizes inventory-moving work; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment; produces Slot Reservation Receipt identifying position/suitability-validation conditions; may retain dimensions. Safety Zone Controller: protected-area restrictions. Fire Alarm Panel: alarm status. Maintenance Release Terminal: availability records. Requirements: valid receipt/safe pallet acceptance; scheduled-window check and unscheduled-arrival review before entry; drivers obey staging instructions; identification/seal verification before unloading authorization. Door/staging/crew availability, coordinated unobstructed yard movement; safe holding until reassignment. Compare physical/paperwork counts, segregate damage; monitor occupancy/clearance; yard personnel notify receiving staff of departure readiness. Pause unsafe/conflicted/equipment-affected unloading. Record counts/inspection/door release before closure/allocation. Allocation considers dimensions/mass/compatibility/retrieval demand; favors short paths for fast movers; restricted-handling positions require approval; preserve pallet/equipment clearances; exclude capacity/status/restriction conflicts. Reservations require position/access-path availability confirmation. Aisle zoning limits conflicts; cranes normally remain assigned aisles; cross-aisle travel requires authorization; commands require valid target/aisle conditions. Conveyor entry requires completed inspection/identification. Reconcile

New part:
S079: It uses conveyor status and transfer-point signals to determine when a pallet can advance.
S080: The Conveyor Line Controller maintains a separate sequence for each active conveyor path.
S081: Conveyor Line Controller is also known as Brasshaven in local operating terminology.
S082: At each transfer point, interlocks prevent movement into a section that is occupied or unavailable.
S083: Presence sensors confirm that a pallet has reached the expected position before a transfer is initiated.
S084: A blocked transfer point holds the affected pallet upstream while other clear paths may continue operating.
S085: Accumulation zones provide controlled spacing between pallets when downstream movement pauses.
S086: Release from an accumulation zone occurs only when the next conveyor section reports ready.
S087: At a merge, the controller grants passage to one approaching pallet at a time.
S088: The Conveyor Line Controller produces the Transfer Induction Ticket for each accepted induction.
S089: Each output record carries the identifiers and routing details needed to associate the induction with its pallet.
S090: The controller checks that required induction fields are present before releasing the pallet from the transfer point.
S091: Duplicate induction requests are held for resolution rather than treated as new pallet movements.
S092: The North Aisle Stacker Crane sends the Aisle Occupancy Snapshot.
S093: The reported aisle condition reflects the crane's current view of occupied and available storage positions.
S094: Changes in reported conditions support safer decisions about whether an induction can proceed.
S095: The North Aisle Stacker Crane updates its reported condition as its operating state changes.
S096: If reporting becomes stale, the affected induction path remains held until current status is available.
S097: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can review persistent holds through established operational procedures.
S098: After a fault is cleared, the controller verifies transfer-point readiness before resuming the held sequence.
S099: Normal sequencing resumes without changing the order of pallets already committed to a transfer path.
S100: Normal sequencing resumes without changing the order of pallets already committed to a transfer path.
S101: Outbound preparation starts when the Warehouse Management System establishes the intended shipment window and loading priorities.
S102: Wave planning accounts for pallet identity, destination, due time, and the available staging positions.
S103: The Warehouse Management System checks that planned pallet moves remain consistent with outbound capacity and current inventory records.
S104: Morrowglass is an operational alias for the Warehouse Management System.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
